item3_stu_con_044.exact_sentence: Use the admitted Prism transform in bounded chunks of at most64pixels, relative-colorimetric/depth32/BPCfalse, with actual profile/engine/options receipts and accounted lifetime. (spec text as stored: the spaces before 64, false and the digits are missing in the file)
item3_stu_con_044.reading: The sentence is addressed to Develop (the caller of the admitted transform): the unit of work is one admitted transform call on at most 64 pixels, each with its own receipts and an accounted lifetime. It names three obligations: (a) chunk <= 64 pixels, (b) per-call profile/engine/options receipts, (c) accounted lifetime. Prism's legacy admitted route already implements the same bound internally (lib.rs and admitted.rs chunks(64)). Two readings: LITERAL = the caller drives one AdmittedWideEngine::transform call per 64 pixels; PRISM-INTERNAL = the admitted conversion itself is evaluated in <= 64-pixel chunks with a per-chunk record, whatever the request or band size
item3_stu_con_044.decision: Implement PRISM-INTERNAL now (cheap, bit-identical, no API break) and price LITERAL; the lead/Operator decides whether PRISM-INTERNAL satisfies the sentence. Not a waiver: with this change develop's tile jobs run on 64-pixel chunks inside Prism; the caller-driven literal form remains possible (AdmittedWideEngine::transform accepts <= 64-pixel requests) and costs the numbers below. If the Operator insists on the literal form, develop must call transform per 64 pixels (serial, one engine) and forfeit prepare_job band parallelism
item3_stu_con_044.implementation: ADMITTED_CHUNK_PIXELS = 64 (wide.rs, was CHUNK_PIXELS 1024) now sizes the chunk loop of WideEngine::compute (transform of WideEngine and AdmittedWideEngine) and of WideJob::convert_band / convert_band_in_place; each chunk starts with a cancellation check, then evaluation, finite-output check and digest update. WideChunkAccount {bound_pixels, chunks, pixels, max_chunk_pixels, scratch_bytes} is recorded per band (WideBandReport::chunks), per request and per job (WideReceipt::chunks; job = merge in band order). The digest staging buffer is one chunk of CMYK values (CHUNK_STAGE_BYTES = 1024 bytes on the band's stack, hoisted out of the per-chunk call); the admitted request lease already charged `CHUNK_PIXELS x out_ch x 4`, which is now 1 KiB instead of 16 KiB. Ledger charging is unchanged: everything is charged in full at prepare and a band charges nothing (tests/wide_job.rs admitted_job_charges_everything_before_the_bands_for_every_thread_count green unchanged)
item3_stu_con_044.what_the_lifetime_record_means: per-chunk lifetime is structural and recorded as counts: a chunk begins at its cancellation check and ends at its digest update before the next chunk of that request/band begins; chunks/pixels/max_chunk_pixels/scratch_bytes are deterministic functions of the band sizes (equal for 1 and 8 threads). Prism-owned per-chunk memory is the 1 KiB stack staging only; chunk pixels live in the caller's band buffers (accounted by their owner) so there is no per-chunk ledger lease
item3_stu_con_044.not_accounted: the stack staging buffer (<= 1024 bytes per in-flight band call) is not a ledger lease; per-chunk RECEIPTS are aggregated (one receipt per request/job with the chunk counts, not one per chunk); the lease sizes are still reasoned bounds (R6 findings[2])
item3_stu_con_044.tests: tests/wide_chunks.rs: chunk_accounting_is_bounded_deterministic_and_allocation_free (band sizes 1/63/64/65/127/128/129/1000/2049 on SRGB->P3 and CMYK table -> sRGB with BPC: per-band, per-request and per-job accounts exact, job account equal for 1 and 8 threads, output bits equal the whole-frame request, ZERO heap allocations inside convert_band and convert_band_in_place measured with a thread-local counting global allocator), cancellation_is_checked_between_chunks_of_at_most_64_pixels (2 Mi-pixel band canceled from another thread at half its reference time: Err(Canceled), converted prefix 996416 px = 15569 x 64, nothing written after it, prefix equals the uninterrupted run), admitted_transform_and_job_report_their_chunks (admitted request 1000 px = 16 chunks, admitted job in two 500-px bands = 16 chunks, ledger live/calls unchanged across band calls, job bits = request bits), ignored bench bench_literal_64_pixel_admitted_calls_against_internal_chunks. item2_gamma_le_0_destination.evidence: icc_eval.rs at d7027c3: from_mox :212-215 (curv count 1: g == 1 -> Identity else Gamma(g), g = 0 accepted), :225 (para type 0 any finite g), Curve::inverse :297-333 (root(y, g) = pow(y, 1/g) for Gamma and para 1-4 exponents); before the fix g = 0 mapped in-gamut linear values to 0 and values above 1 to inf (NonfiniteOutput), g < 0 gave device values above 1; types 1-4 refused only a = 0
item2_gamma_le_0_destination.basis: ICC.1:2022 (archive.color.org/specification/ICC.1-2022-05.pdf, text via pdftotext): Annex F.2 (grayTRC, p.101) and F.3 (red/green/blueTRC, p.102): a constant one-dimensional curve cannot be inverted and the inverse of a non-invertible curve is undefined; clause 10.6 (curveType, p.48): n = 1 is gamma as u8Fixed8 (so g = 0 is a constant curve y = 1); clause 10.18 (parametricCurveType, p.70-71): domain and range [0,1], values outside are clipped (so g < 0 is the constant 1)
item2_gamma_le_0_destination.fix: Curve::require_invertible (icc_eval.rs) refuses Gamma(g) and para types 1-4 with g <= 0 and constant tables; called for the matrix and Gray TRCs in icc_eval::from_pcs, so it fires when the plan is built (before the cache is touched, before BPC/absolute, fused and staged alike, plain/admitted/job); new typed WideError::NonInvertibleCurve code non_invertible_curve (Observe outcome Unsupported); the same curves remain valid as sources
